content.text:
Fixed and both tests pass. 

The bug was in `parse_flags` at `repo/cli.py:15` — the flag name was taken as everything after `--` without splitting on `=`, so `--out=log.txt` produced `{"out=log.txt": True}`. Now it splits on the first `=` and stores the value directly, without consuming the next arg:

```14:22:/Users/psudokit/benchmark/runs/20261016-105350-g2-kimi-k3-T050-cli-vague-prompt-r0/work/repo/cli.py
        if a.startswith("--"):
            name = a[2:]
            if "=" in name:
                name, value = name.split("=", 1)
                out[name] = value
                i += 1
                continue
            if i + 1 < len(args) and not args[i + 1].startswith("--"):
                out[name] = args[i + 1]
```

Using `split("=", 1)` also handles values containing `=` (e.g. `--query=a=b` → `{"query": "a=b"}`), and `--key=` yields an empty string value.
